svg.text: Perfboard hub: Raspberry Pi 4 ↔ SNES pad 1 ↔ SNES pad 2
Single-pad perfboard (no copper strips). 16 pads, 6 straight wire runs, no crossings. Top view; wires are drawn as if seen through the board.
Coloured pad = used. Plain hole = unused. Dashed ring = optional 100 nF ceramic cap C1 across the 3V3 and GND wires (legs span 4 holes).
Green dashed box = 1×6 male pin header at C4–H4. One 1×6 Dupont female housing (or ribbon) plugs onto it and onto Pi pins 9–19 in the same order (pin 9 = GND at C4).
Colours = your cord's wire colours: green 3.3 V power (pin 1), yellow CLOCK (2), white LATCH (3), red DATA (4, NOT power), black GND (7).
Wire list: 6 wires, all straight along one row
Pi GPIO17 to pad 1 only (D24 stays empty)
Pi GPIO10 to pad 2 only (H14 stays empty)
1. Use insulated wire (26–30 AWG) on the solder side. Rows are only 2.54 mm apart, so bare wire can short 3V3 to GND if it sags.
2. Pad cables: cut the extension cord and solder each wire to the pad of the same colour (pad 1 = C14–G14, pad 2 = C24 and E24–H24). Pins 5 and 6 stay unconnected.
3. GREEN (pin 1) is 3.3 V power and goes to the 3V3 row (G). RED (pin 4) is DATA, NOT power. Pad labels show the SNES pin number; confirm colours with a continuity test.
4. Tie each cord to a spare hole (for example B16 or B26) so pulling the cable never tears a pad.
5. Before connecting the Pi: beep out 3V3 (row G) against GND (row C). There must be no connection. Then check every row for stray bridges to its neighbours.
